1. PASS | app/login/page.tsx implements sign-up form with email/password and role selection, calling AuthContext.signUp.
2. PASS | app/login/page.tsx includes a role selector (patient/pharmacist) passed to AuthContext.signUp for role persistence.
3. PASS | app/login/page.tsx implements sign-in form calling AuthContext.signIn with email/password.
4. PASS | app/dashboard/page.tsx includes a "Sign Out" button calling useAuth().signOut.
5. PASS | supabase_schema.sql defines tables for profiles, medications, orders, order_items, and messages with RLS.
6. PASS | PatientHome component in app/dashboard/page.tsx renders medication list with search input filtering by name.
7. PASS | PatientHome component calls addToCart from CartContext to add medications to the shopping cart.
8. PASS | DashboardPage.handlePlaceOrder creates order and order_items in DB and clears cart.
9. PASS | PatientOrders component in app/dashboard/page.tsx lists orders for the current user.
10. PASS | PatientOrders displays status badges; DashboardPage subscribes to real-time order updates for the user.
11. PASS | PharmacistOrders component in app/dashboard/page.tsx lists all orders for pharmacist management.
12. PASS | PharmacistOrders provides buttons to update order status (pending->processing, etc.) via API.
13. PASS | PharmacistInventory component in app/dashboard/page.tsx lists medications with stock levels.
14. PASS | PharmacistInventory filters and displays low-stock alerts (stock < 10) at the top of the view.
15. PASS | PharmacistInventory has a toggle button to update is_active status, hiding items from patients.
16. PASS | All data (orders, inventory, users) is persisted in Supabase PostgreSQL via the defined schema and API calls.
17. PASS | PharmacistMessages component is only rendered when user.role === 'pharmacist' in DashboardPage.
18. PASS | PharmacistMessages lists other pharmacists from profiles table for selection to start a conversation.
19. PASS | DashboardPage subscribes to Supabase Realtime 'INSERT' events on messages table to update UI instantly.
20. PASS | PharmacistMessages displays sender name (via lookup) and timestamp for each message bubble.
21. PASS | PharmacistMessages fetches initial messages and appends new ones, maintaining conversation history.
22. FAIL | Email sending is implemented in app/api/orders/[id]/route.ts, but the dashboard status update buttons do not call this API; they update DB directly without triggering emails.
23. FAIL | Since the email API is not called by the UI (see #22), the email content details (order ID, meds, status) are not delivered to patients.
24. FAIL | The UI updates order status directly in the database, bypassing the API route that sends emails, so emails are not sent promptly.
25. FAIL | The email API route is not invoked by the frontend, so the email best practices defined in the route are not executed for status changes.

rubric.2: Application implements user registration supporting patient and pharmacist roles.
rubric.5: Application persists all medications, inventory levels, orders, and user accounts using durable, database-backed storage.
rubric.6: Application allows patients to browse available medications with search and filter capabilities.
rubric.7: Application allows patients to add selected medications to a shopping cart.
rubric.8: Application allows patients to place prescription orders from the contents of their cart.
rubric.9: Application allows patients to view a complete history of their past orders.
rubric.10: Application displays real-time order status for patients, including states such as pending, processing, ready for pickup, and completed.
rubric.11: Application provides a pharmacist dashboard for reviewing and managing incoming orders.
rubric.12: Application allows pharmacists to update the status of each order.
rubric.13: Application allows pharmacists to view and manage current inventory levels for all medications.
rubric.14: Application generates low-stock alerts for pharmacists when inventory levels fall below defined thresholds.
rubric.15: Application allows pharmacists to mark specific items as out of stock so patients cannot order them.
rubric.16: Application persists all order, inventory, and status data in the database to ensure full durability across sessions.
rubric.17: Application provides a private messaging interface that is accessible only to authenticated pharmacists.
rubric.18: Application allows pharmacists to search for and select another pharmacist to start a private conversation.
rubric.19: Application ensures pharmacist-to-pharmacist messages are delivered and displayed in real time to both parties without requiring a page refresh.
rubric.20: Application displays clear sender attribution, including name and role, along with timestamps for each message in every private conversation.
rubric.21: Application maintains a conversation history for each private pharmacist thread so prior messages can be reviewed.
rubric.22: Application sends an automatic email notification to the patient whenever their prescription order status changes.
rubric.23: Application includes key details in each notification email, such as order identifier, medication summary, previous status, and new status.
rubric.24: Application ensures that notification emails are sent reliably and promptly immediately after each order status update is saved in the system.
rubric.25: Application follows basic email best practices for all notifications, including a clear subject line indicating the update and appropriate sender information.
